blocks.prompt: 11. Let \(f\) be continuous and suppose: \(\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\,dx = 10\) and \(\int_{2}^{4} f(x)\,dx = 6\). If the average value of \(f\) on \([0, 3]\) equals the average value on \([3, 4]\), find \(\int_{3}^{4} f(x)\,dx\).
blocks.explanation:
Two unknown pieces: \(A = \int_2^3 f\) and \(B = \int_3^4 f\), with \(A + B = 6\).
Plan: write both averages in terms of \(A\) and \(B\), set them equal, and solve with \(A + B = 6\).
steps:
The two averages
\[f_{\text{av}}[0, 3] = \dfrac{10 + A}{3}, \qquad f_{\text{av}}[3, 4] = \dfrac{B}{1} = B\]

Set them equal and use \(A = 6 - B\)
\[\dfrac{10 + A}{3} = B\]
\[10 + (6 - B) = 3B\]
\[16 = 4B \Rightarrow B = 4\]
Why: one equation in one unknown after substituting \(A = 6 - B\).
